page: Microsoft Azure F64-16amds_v7 is an x86_64 virtual instance configured with 16 dedicated physical cores running on an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked up to 4.5 GHz, managed via Microsoft Hyper-V. The system provides 1 thread per core with dedicated CPU allocation, backed by 48 KB L1d, 1 MB L2, and 32 MB L3 cache. It incorporates vector instruction extensions including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and BF16, alongside cryptographic acceleration instructions like AES and VAES.

The hardware configuration provides 512 GB of system memory, delivering a dense 32 GB of RAM per vCPU, alongside 7,560 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage. There are no discrete hardware GPUs attached. In synthetic testing, the single-core CPU throughput registers in the top 10% tier via stress-ng, supported by high single-threaded compression performance (41.04 GB/sec in gzip and 17.94 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression). PassMark memory benchmarking also reflects strong throughput, while multi-core compute tests settle in the median tier due to the 16-core allocation.

With 512 GB of RAM coupled with over 7.5 TB of local NVMe storage against 16 dedicated cores, this configuration trades wide parallel compute scaling for exceptional per-core memory capacity and local I/O bandwidth. It suits memory-intensive enterprise databases, large-scale caching instances, in-memory analytical workloads, and data pipelines requiring rapid local scratch space without requiring massive thread concurrency.
description: Microsoft Azure F64-16amds_v7 is an x86_64 compute instance powered by a dedicated 16-core AMD EPYC 9V45 processor operating at up to 4.5 GHz on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. Designed with an expansive 512 GB of memory, the system delivers an uncommon 32 GB of RAM per physical core, complemented by 7,560 GB of fast local NVMe SSD storage and zero GPU accelerators. In benchmark evaluations, the server achieves top-tier single-core performance and rapid single-threaded compression throughput, while overall multi-core and database processing scores remain balanced within the median tier. Hardware features include AVX-512 vector extensions with VNNI and BF16 support alongside native cryptographic acceleration. This hardware configuration is particularly suited for memory-bound relational databases, in-memory data processing, caching clusters, and ETL workloads that require substantial per-thread RAM capacity and massive local NVMe disk space.
